description.summary: where an application's icon is shown

protocol.description:
This protocol lets a launcher, such as a dock, tell the compositor where it shows the icon of an application. The compositor uses the icon as the spatial origin of that application's windows: a window launched from the icon grows out of it, and a window that is minimized or closed shrinks back into it.
Applications are identified by the app_id their toplevels set, compared without regard to ASCII case.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_app_icon_manager_v1
interface.description: A global factory for crownos_app_icon_v1 objects.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Icons created through it are unaffected.

request.name: get_app_icon

description.summary: show an application's icon on a surface

request.description:
Create an icon for the application app_id, drawn on surface. A surface may carry the icons of any number of applications, and an application may have icons on several surfaces; the compositor uses the one on the output the window is on.
The icon has no rectangle until set_rectangle is called, and until then the compositor does not use it.

interface.name: crownos_app_icon_v1
interface.description:
The icon of one application on one surface.
If the wl_surface is destroyed, this object becomes inert.

entry.name: invalid_rectangle
entry.summary: width or height is not positive, or the radius is negative

request.name: destroy

description.summary: the icon is no longer shown

request.description: Destroy the icon. Windows of the application no longer grow out of or shrink into it.

request.name: set_rectangle
request.description:
Set the rectangle the icon occupies, in surface-local coordinates, and the radius of its rounded corners. This is where the icon rests when the surface is fully shown: a surface that slides itself out of view does not need to update it.
Takes effect immediately.

request.name: activate
request.description:
The user clicked or tapped the icon.
If the application has windows, the compositor restores the ones that are minimized, growing them out of the icon, and focuses the most recent one. Otherwise it replies with the launch event, and the launcher is expected to start the application.

event.name: launch
event.description: The application has no window: the launcher should start it. The first window of the application that is mapped shortly after grows out of this icon.
